Find lines a note says are contained in another line

Source: R/check_inclusion.R
check_inclusion.Rd

A function-based income statement reports administrative expenses, distribution costs and staff costs as separate figures. They are not always separate amounts: where the staff note says the wages were expensed under administration, the staff costs are inside the administrative expenses, and adding the two counts them twice.

Usage

check_inclusion(
  x,
  note = "DisclosureOfEmployeeBenefitsExpense",
  within = c("AdministrativeExpenses", "DistributionCosts", "CostOfSales")
)

Arguments

x

A tibble from read_xbrl().

note

The text block to read. Defaults to the staff cost note.

within

Elements the note may place the costs under. Defaults to the two function-based expense lines.

Value

A tibble with one row per line the note places inside another: elementid (the contained line), within (the containing line), value and within_value where both are reported, sole (whether the note names this destination alone), and evidence, the sentence the reading rests on. No rows where the note says nothing.

Why no other check sees it

Both figures are correctly tagged, both belong to the statement, and the statement still adds up – because the filer only ever counted the money once. Nothing structural distinguishes this from a filing where the two are genuinely separate. The only place the difference is stated is the prose of the note.

How common it is

Rare, in Danish filings. Across 4,304 filings from 2020-2024, 87 use the function-based income statement at all, 38 report administrative expenses and staff costs together, and 3 carry a note naming administration. Most Danish companies file by nature – gross profit, then staff costs, then depreciation – where the question does not arise.

That is worth knowing before relying on this: it is a check for a small, real population, not a widespread correction.

A cost split between destinations

A note may name several: wages expensed partly under production and partly under administration. Each is returned as a row with sole = FALSE, because the note says where the money went without saying how much went to each. Treating such a filing as though the whole staff cost sat in administration would replace one error with another, so nothing is apportioned.

What it does not do

It reports the inclusion; it does not net it out. How to handle a double-counted line depends on which variable a statistic is building – an employment cost total wants the staff figure, an operating cost breakdown wants administration less staff – and that is the caller's decision.

See also

xbrl_note_tables(), which reads the same notes for their figures rather than their prose.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
x <- read_xbrl("filing.xml")
check_inclusion(x)
} # }
